entities.summary:
Petrus Nannius was a Dutch poet, accomplished Latin scholar and humanist of the 16th century. A contemporary of Desiderius Erasmus, he was born in Alkmaar and was an important figure in the humanism of the time, having provided a foundation with his teaching for the later flowering of humanism in the region.

Nannius's most notable work was 'De Natura Rerum,' a comprehensive treatise on natural philosophy, which influenced thinkers such as Francis Bacon and René Descartes. He also contributed to the translation of ancient Greek texts, playing a crucial role in the revival of classical learning during the Renaissance.

Petrus Nannius's legacy extends beyond the realm of humanism, as his emphasis on empirical observation and experimental methods in natural philosophy paved the way for the scientific revolution of the 17th century.

The Dutch humanist's life was cut short when he died on July 31, 1557, but his intellectual contributions continue to shape our understanding of the natural world and the foundations of modern science.

In the words of Nannius himself, 'Scientia est rerum cognitio,' or 'Knowledge is the recognition of things,' a sentiment that encapsulates the essence of his philosophical endeavors.
